newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish state to sell more Tele Danmark.
newsitem.headline: Danish state to sell more Tele Danmark.

text.p: The Danish state is to sell all or part of its remaining 52 percent stake in telecoms group Tele Danmark, the research ministry said on Wednesday.
It gave no date for the sale and said that minister Jytte Hylden would present a firm proposal this autumn.
"Now that legislation on the telecommunications industry is complete, it is natural to take up the question of the state's ownership up," a ministry statement quoted Hylden as saying.

"It is important that a sale of the state's shares take place in the best possible way for both the state and Tele Danmark. I therefore will in the autumn launch an initiative for political action on a share sale," she said.
Tele Danmark was partially privatised in 1994 and the government, pledged to balance its budget and cut foreign debt, has said that it does not intend to retain its holding indefinitely.
The Danish telecommunications industry was deregulated last year and several foreign competitors are building up a local presence, among them Sweden's Telia and France Telecom
Recent market talk said that British Telecommunications was eyeing a stake in Tele Danmark but the Danish group on June 6 said it had heard nothing from B.T.
Shortly after the Danish government announcement Tele Danmark's share traded at 342.00 crowns, three crowns down on Tuesday's close. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650
